title: Bounded Walk Loop Invariant
statement: Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $R$ be a relation on natural numbers, and let $b$ be a Boolean value. Let $Q$ be a proposition and let $\sigma$ be a state whose registers are all at most $B$. Write $w_b=\sigma.u$ and $q_b=\sigma.i$ when $b$ is true, and $w_b=\sigma.v$ and $q_b=\sigma.i1$ otherwise. Suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.cur<\sigma.K$, and $\sigma.stp\le q_b$. If, whenever there is a walk from $\sigma.cur$ to $w_b$ of at most $q_b-\sigma.stp$ steps, with each intermediate vertex less than $\sigma.K$ and each step in $R$, the machine started at its walk-entry state with $cur=stp=g=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine started at its walk-loop state with register values $\sigma$ terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when both such a walk exists and $Q$ holds.
hypotheses_covered: Every register of $\sigma$ is at most $B$
The stated implication from walk existence to the semantics at the walk-entry state
replaced:
Let $E,B\in\mathbb{N}$, let $x$ be a finite binary word, let $\mathcal O$ be an oracle,
let $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$, let $Q$ be a proposition, and let $\sigma$
be a register state with every register at most $B$. Write $R(u,v)$ for the truth of the
oracle's type-$3$ query on $(x,u,v,\sigma.s)$, and let $\operatorname{Walk}_{j}(c,t)$
mean that there is an $R$-walk from $c$ to $t$ of at most $j$ steps, with each
intermediate vertex less than $\sigma.K$. Define the target $w(b)$ to be $\sigma.u$ if
$b$ is true and $\sigma.v$ otherwise, and the step bound $q(b)$ to be $\sigma.i$ if $b$
is true and $\sigma.i1$ otherwise. Suppose $\sigma.K+1\le B$, $\sigma.cur<\sigma.K$, and
$\sigma.stp\le q(b)$. If the existence of a walk of at most $q(b)-\sigma.stp$ steps from
$\sigma.cur$ to $w(b)$ implies that the machine initialized at the corresponding
walk-initialization stage with $cur=stp=g=0$ terminates within register bound $B$ and
accepts exactly when $Q$ holds, then the machine initialized at the walk-loop stage with
state $\sigma$ terminates within that bound and accepts exactly when both such a walk
exists and $Q$ holds.
